qs.q: A 45-year-old woman with a 3-cm unifocal breast cancer undergoes wide local excision with a 1-cm margin of normal tissue. What is an absolute requirement following this specific breast-conserving surgery?
o: Axillary clearance of level III nodes
qs.e: Breast-conserving surgery (wide local excision) must always be followed by radiotherapy to the breast to achieve survival rates equivalent to mastectomy. Modified radical mastectomy is a separate alternative surgical approach, not a follow-up step.
qs.s: Breast Lumps and Breast Cancer: Triple Assessment, Staging and: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following clinical scenarios represents an absolute contraindication to breast-conserving surgery (wide local excision)?
o: Patient preference for preserving the native breast
Tumour location in the upper outer quadrant
Multicentric or widespread disease in the breast
A single small tumour measuring 3 cm in diameter
qs.e: Multicentric or widespread disease is a contraindication to breast-conserving surgery, which requires a single small tumour. A 3-cm tumour in a suitable breast can be managed with breast conservation if margins are clear.
qs.s: Breast Lumps and Breast Cancer: Triple Assessment, Staging and: MCQs

qs.q: A surgical resident prepares to excise a biopsy-proven melanoma. Why is it strictly recommended to avoid performing a wide local excision before obtaining a definitive histological diagnosis via narrow biopsy?
o: The precise Breslow thickness is required to plan the correct surgical margins
Wide excision prior to diagnosis accelerates distant brain metastasis
It completely eliminates the regional lymph nodes from being palpable
Primary closure becomes anatomically impossible without prior shave biopsy
qs.e: The Breslow thickness obtained from the initial diagnosis determines the exact wide local excision margins required for the definitive operation. Performing a wide excision prematurely alters tissue planes and obscures prognostic depth assessment.
qs.s: Malignant Melanoma and Skin Cancer: ABCDE, Breslow Thickness and Wide: MCQs

qs.q: A 52-year-old woman is diagnosed with a cutaneous melanoma on her forearm. Histological examination reveals a Breslow thickness of 0.8 mm without ulceration. What is the recommended wide local excision margin for this primary lesion?
qs.e: A Breslow thickness of up to 1 mm requires a 1 cm wide local excision margin. In situ lesions require 0.5 cm, whereas thicker lesions require 1 to 2 cm or 2 cm margins.
qs.s: Malignant Melanoma and Skin Cancer: ABCDE, Breslow Thickness and Wide: MCQs
